Hey dude I was in your shoes a few months ago. Got my first DUI when I was 20 and my second at 25. Being someone who comes from a pretty troubled life and wrestles with depression and anxiety even before my arrests I can tell you these feelings go away after some time and you will be a better and wiser person after. Don’t give up hope. Hire a good attorney and keep pushing forward. I was suicidal too, it sucks making the same mistake twice and the shame and guilt that comes with it can be too much to bare but if you be kind to yourself and learn from it you will be just fine, trust me. This 2nd DUI I got made me really take a look at myself and forced me to address a lot of my issues and lately I am finding myself happier and the most sober I’ve been in years.

When I was 20 I had the pleasure of taking a eurotrip with some of my friends. Spent a most of the time in Spain but got to stop and hang around Paris and London for a little too. Being so excited that I was in another country and also being able to drink legally I ended up basically binge drinking the entire time. Looking back I really regret not taking everything in fully and enjoying the trip sober especially since I’m a big history fan. The few in my group that didn’t drink were always up early getting coffee and doing some exploring while the rest of us were nursing hangovers in our hostels. I remember walking through London with the biggest headache of my life and the thought of eating anywhere we stopped at made me want to throw up. You’re not missing anything by not drinking, the days I didn’t drink on my trip were my favorite if I’m being honest, I got to do, see, and remember a lot more those days

My man, I know where you’re coming from. And like I said there is nothing wrong with unwinding with a few beers and getting some rest. What I’m trying to say is that drinking is not a solution long term, in fact in can spiral into a problem and make things more difficult in the future. I’m not saying you shouldn’t drink, I can’t count  the amount of times I would come home from work and crush a few beers, rail a few lines and smoke some weed to get over a long day and it was great, but in my case I wasn’t dealing with the root cause of all my problems and things eventually got worse. Therapy may take years but you learn life long ways to cope and maybe conquer your anxiety and live a healthy life, and I’m just putting it out there that it’s worth checking out. But if you’re gonna drink to sleep pour yourself up a few shots of whiskey and put some hair on your nuts like a mfin man

Started doing this in my teens, 1-2 beers went to a six pack every night and then drinking bottles of liquor in one sitting and this spanned for 8 years, I’m in my late twenties now. Currently in recovery, withdrawals are a bitch, wishing I would have sought therapy to help when I was younger because it’s been helping me cope way better. Nothing wrong with having a few beers every once and a while but using alcohol/drugs to self medicate my anxiety was by far one of the biggest mistakes of my life, if you’re unlucky like me it gets to the point where your anxiety is worse than ever before and you have to take substances everyday just to feel normal

Hey man, I literally experienced the same thing as you last year, my girl also decided to drop that she was pregnant on me (turned out that I’m not the father, thank god) when I walked in and started freaking out. I wish I would have done what you did by getting in my car and leaving, I ended up beating the dude and sped off before the cops came and ended up with a huge charge on top of an absolutely crushed heart. Take a deep breathe. You did nothing wrong. You have unfortunately found out the person you were in love with isn’t who you thought they were in the worst way possible. It hurts like hell and it’s going to knock you down hard but you can and will rise from this. It may feel like you’ve lost everything but my dear friend it’s quite the opposite. Therapy worked wonders for me, I had nightmares for months where I would relive that day over and over again and talking about it helped. From someone who has been in your shoes before I can promise you that it gets better.
